news.title: This Is The Very Best Week Of The Year To Buy A House
news.summary: This Is The Very Best Week Of The Year To Buy A House
news.full_text:
The week spanning September 27 through October 3 is historically the best time to buy a home, with inventory up 32% and 5.7% of listings seeing price reductions.

High mortgage rates around 6.7% have thinned buyer competition, giving remaining buyers more negotiating power against motivated sellers.

A K-shaped housing market is emerging: sub-$300K home sales fell 10% this year while million-dollar listings held steady.

Read More: Learn 7 secret wealth tips high net worth investors use that most investors miss (sponsor)

If you can afford it, the best week of the year to buy a house is from September 27 to October 3. This, of course, depends on whether you can pay cash or take on a 6.7% fixed-rate, 30-year mortgage. Many people can't, which has triggered a major slowdown in housing sales.

"Historically, this week offers the most favorable balance of market conditions for buyers. Inventory tends to be elevated, prices typically dip below their seasonal peak, buyer competition slows, and the overall pace of the market becomes more manageable," Realtor.com reports. Of course, for some sellers, it could signal desperation. Summer is a good time to sell a house in most parts of the country. For sellers who didn't have luck, it could be a time to reprice and negotiate.

Supply and demand numbers compare favorably to the start of the year for home buyers. In most years, inventory is up 31.9% compared to the start of the year.

The real estate research firm says that this week, the number of buyers in the market has dipped compared to most weeks. It is simple supply and demand. High interest rates may have driven those buyers out of the market. In that case, the current situation could continue. Additionally, evidence suggests sellers have modestly dropped prices from their average of $416,000, which is near a record.

news.title: Assemblin Caverion prints €1.5B floating-rate note in bumper day for European high yield
news.summary: Assemblin Caverion prints €1.5B floating-rate note in bumper day for European high yield
news.full_text:
Assemblin Caverion on Sept. 16 priced the second-largest euro-denominated floating-rate note (FRN) ever sold by a European high yield borrower, after the Stockholm-based technical installations group upsized its planned seven-year deal to €1.53 billion.

The bumper deal — which cleared at E+300, offered at par — is the largest euro FRN tranche since Wind Tre's record-breaking €2.25 billion deal back in 2017. It tops a €1.375 billion Nexi bond from 2018 and a €1.25 billion trade from TeamSystem last year.

Big slateAssemblin Caverion's offering was also the largest in a €4.53 billion slate of high yield transactions to price on Sept. 16 — which according to LCD, represents the busiest day of the year so far in volume terms for the European primary high yield market, and the sixth-busiest on record.

The mammoth size of the new offering for Assemblin Caverion mainly reflects the fact that the group is effectively merging a higher-cost €780 million E+350 FRN into the new tranche, a strategy commonly used by high yield borrowers whose existing debt is already callable.

The deal, originally sized at €750 million, nevertheless reflects strong demand for floating-rate paper from an issuer that already has both fixed- and floating-rate debt in its structure.

"We were surprised seeing FRNs only, but it is the environment we prefer as an investor," said a manager at a high yield bond fund. He also said the fund has increased its allocation to floating-rate debt from 15% to about 20% in recent weeks, and plans to increase this allocation to roughly a quarter of the portfolio.

FRN buyersThe creation of new European CLOs — the core buyers of high yield FRNs — has meanwhile remained robust this year, with new issuance running roughly in line with 2025's record volumes and new managers entering the market. While the number of warehouses open at any given time is difficult to quantify, speakers at S&P Global's European Structured Finance Conference in September put the number at 200.

Assemblin Caverion was formed in 2024 after Triton merged its technical installations company Assemblin with Caverion, the Finnish construction systems group which the private equity firm took private the prior year for €1.12 billion. The bond deal will support a dividend to Triton.

news.title: Corning Just Signed a Multibillion-Dollar Fiber Deal for AI and Broadband With Verizon. What That Means for GLW Stock.
news.summary: Corning Just Signed a Multibillion-Dollar Fiber Deal for AI and Broadband With Verizon. What That Means for GLW Stock.
news.full_text:
Corning (GLW) is now home to another massive fiber deal. On Sept. 8, Verizon (VZ) struck a multibillion-dollar supply agreement with Corning for more than 80 million miles of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions through 2032. Fiber not only supports Verizon's broadband initiative but is needed for the construction of the long-haul, low-latency network necessary to link artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

The timing is particularly fortuitous for Corning. The company already has a multibillion-dollar deal in place with Amazon (AMZN), as well as an initiative tied to Nvidia's (NVDA) AI infrastructure construction. Simply put, Corning is gaining traction in several different layers of the network, both inside and outside AI data centers.

Corning is a materials science corporation with its headquarters in Corning, New York. The company specializes in glass, ceramics, optical physics, and manufacturing. Corning offers its products in optical communications, mobile consumer electronics, displays, automotive, and other areas. Currently, Corning has a market capitalization of approximately $124 billion.

GLW stock currently trades near the $148 level. Although the stock is trading about 45% below its 52-week high of $271.78, shares still have appreciated about 70% year-to-date (YTD). This beats the S&P 500 Index ($SPX) over the same period, which has gained roughly 11% so far in 2026. GLW stock has also almost doubled from its 52-week low of $77.05.

All this performance leaves Corning with a tough valuation profile. GLW stock trades at about 43.7 times forward earnings and 7.9 times sales. But there are some fundamental reasons behind this valuation premium, because Corning recently won another big customer. Indeed, the new agreement with Verizon comes after a multibillion-dollar contract with Amazon. The company also has a partnership with Nvidia for the expansion of U.S. optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10 times and fiber production capacity by more than 50%.

Corning pays a quarterly dividend of $0.28 per share, providing a yield of roughly 0.8% at the latest share price. The next dividend payment will be made on Sept. 29 to shareholders of record on Aug. 31.

Corning reported a strong second quarter. Core sales rose 17% year-over-year (YOY) to $4.74 billion, while core EPS jumped 30% to $0.78. Earnings beat the $0.76 consensus estimate, while revenue came in above the $4.63 billion forecast. On a GAAP basis, sales were $4.51 billion, and GAAP EPS rose 19% to $0.64.

Of course, what matters even more for the AI investment thesis is that Optical Communications sales grew 32% YOY to $2.07 billion in Q2. Within that, Enterprise Networks revenue skyrocketed 65%, "with Gen AI product sales growing significantly faster." Core operating margin expanded by 190 basis points to 20.9%, while adjusted free cash flow stood at $1.42 billion.
